name: Calm / stable harmony
harmonyTendencies: subdominant-minor as a soft borrowed color
dominant tension is often reduced in the source examples
arrangementTendencies: Longer chord holds can support a calm impression; avoid excessive dominant tension
The author also notes that melody, arrangement and other musical elements affect the result

source.title: 落ち着いた雰囲気を持つコード進行を考える
source.author: 内山敦支

notes: Paraphrases the examples and listening interpretation in Uchiyama's article. These are the author's examples and interpretation; do not infer mood from chords alone.

name: Chord progression affect and groove (research)
harmonyTendencies: In the study's stimuli, progressions judged happier were more likely to elicit groove than sadder progressions.
arrangementTendencies: Drum-break accompaniment increased groove ratings for both happy and sad progressions.

source.title: Is happier music groovier? The influence of emotional characteristics of musical chord progressions on groove
source.author: Satoshi Kawase

notes: Single study with professionally composed drum-break stimuli; results should not be generalized to every genre or listener.

name: Swing and microtiming are style-dependent (research)
arrangementTendencies: Swing ratio and small timing deviations are separate from tempo.
Microtiming patterns can be genre-specific; do not apply a fixed swing or random timing offset to every track.

source.title: Microtiming Deviations and Swing Feel in Jazz
source.author: George Datseris et al.

notes: The study found quantized versions rated slightly higher for swing than originals across the tested jazz recordings, while expanded microtiming deviations rated lower. This does not mean quantization always grooves better; it cautions against exaggerating timing offsets.

name: Tonic-relative interval color map
harmonyTendencies: 1st: tonal center and strongest reference point.
3rd: major/minor quality; a central source of tonal color.
5th: stable structural tone in common triadic harmony.
2nd/9th and 6th/13th: color tones that can add openness or extension.
4th/11th: suspended or unresolved color when placed against the 3rd.
Major 7th and minor 2nd: close semitone relations to the tonic; often create strong directional tension.
Tritone: high intervallic tension, often associated with dominant function in tonal contexts.
arrangementTendencies: Display scale membership separately from interval character.
Use color as a theory-oriented tendency, not as a deterministic emotion label.
notes: App visualization heuristic based on conventional interval and chord-function descriptions. It describes tonal roles relative to the selected tonic; perceived mood also depends on melody, rhythm, register, timbre and context.
